post.caption:
Drift velocity in a household wire is on the order of millimetres per second, so at that pace an electron would take hours to reach the bulb. The light is instant because the electromagnetic field propagates at close to light speed, and the energy travels in the field around the wire rather than inside it. The water-pipe analogy misses this. A bicycle chain is closer: push one link and the whole loop moves at once.
